title: Riso road

reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Flat ink plates, each fed through 2 px off the last, every one mottled by a grain smeared 1 px along the feed, under a 3 px black key: a road at 32°, a lightning stripe, two Mindgut robots racing.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 1440 × 1920 and every length scales with the canvas

angle.does: Slope of the road and the wall across the sheet. Measured 32°.

wall.does: Where the pink wall meets the road at the left edge.

curb.does: Width of the lighter strip along the wall, 40 px at 1. 0 removes it.

lane.does: Distance of the lightning stripe from the wall.

stripes.does: One or two lightning stripes along the road.

stripeW.does: Width of the yellow band, 70 px at 1.

robotSize.does: Height of the two racers, 380 px at 1.

smoke.does: Size of the puff clouds behind each racer. 0 removes them.

stars.does: Sparkle marks thrown around each racer.

key.does: Width of the black line. Measured 2.8 px.

grain.does: Mottle of every ink. Measured σ 6 on the gray, 8 on the pink.

streak.does: How far the grain is smeared along the drum feed. The gray's autocorrelation runs 0.60 along x and 0.42 along y.

rough.does: How much the grain breaks every plate edge and the key.

misreg.does: Offset between plates, each in its own direction, as the paper shifts between passes.

seed.does: Re-rolls clouds, stars and the grain.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Open road: σ 6 grain smeared 1 px along the feed

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Stripe edge: paper shows between key and yellow, the plates 2.5 px apart

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Green racer: a flat plate under the key, 3 px off

pass_order: geometry: a road direction at 32°, the wall line, the curb strip, the lightning stripes as zigzag bands with pointed ends
object plate by id: puff clouds (circles stroked on the key, filled and cut from the key so only the outer scallop stays), two robots, star marks, motion ticks
one grain: a hashed field blurred 0.45 px and smeared 1 px along the feed
per pixel: paper, road plate, wall plate, curb, stripe plate, object inks, each sampled at its own offset, each edge broken by the grain, each tone mottled by it; the key last at its own offset

measured.grain_autocorr: clean gray plate: x 0.60, 0.16; y 0.42, 0.04 (slightly longer along x)
measured.misregistration_px: 2 to 3, read on the stripe edge where paper shows between key and yellow
measured.rejected: a strongly streaked grain: the first patch measured 0.89 along x, but it held a stripe edge; the clean gray reads 0.60 against 0.42

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Riso set palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The scene is generated; render-side windows were placed with search.py after the 2026-11-12 robot redraw. Patches sit on the same ink in both: open road gray, the pink wall, a stripe edge with its key, a smoke cloud edge, the whole sheet for ink shares.

limits: Benchmark 90.8 % mean. The stripe-edge patch scores lowest (histogram 56 %, contrast 55 %): the reference patch holds a stripe edge, a star and a corner of the dark green car, so its key class is 15 % and reads as the car's green; the rebuild's patch holds one stripe edge with 3 % key.
Whole-plate gray coverage (75 %) is higher than the reference because two robots cover less road than two cars.
The reference's two cars are not redrawn; two Mindgut robots race in their place with the same key, smoke and star marks.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
